Maya (CSM): Heads-up — Meridian asked for a one-page SLO summary + a worked credit demo for their finance team. Go-live Friday. Can SRE/Eng drop numbers + a short example?
Ethan (SRE): Yep. Contract states 99.5% monthly availability and p95 < 300ms. I'll pull 30d availability and flag any day < 99.3%.
Nora (Eng): I'll export route-level p95s and include per-region splits. Also a line about fallback routing adding ~40ms tail.
Ravi (Enablement): I'll turn this into a single-page PDF + short FAQ. Want the worked credit calculation in plain English.
Maya (CSM): Legal requests definition: "downtime" = any 5m window where availability < target. Also p95 computed per UTC day.
Ethan (SRE): SQL I'll run (simplified): ```sql
SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as day, 1 - sum(downtime_ms)/86400000.0 as availability
FROM infra.uptime_events
WHERE customer_id='meridian' AND ts > now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY day;
```
Nora (Eng): p95 sample: {"route":"/v1/infer","period":"2024-02-01:2024-03-02","p95_ms":288}. I'll include JSON per region.
Maya (CSM): Worked credit example request: show math for a 30-day billing period where availability = 99.2 (target 99.5).
Ethan (SRE): Plain calc: 30 days = 43,200 minutes. Target 99.5% => allowed downtime = 0.5% * 43,200 = 216 minutes. Observed availability 99.2% => downtime = 0.8% * 43,200 = 345.6 minutes. Minutes below target = 345.6 - 216 = 129.6 minutes. If credit = (minutes below / total minutes)*invoice_amount and cap = 10% (example), then credit% = 129.6/43,200 ≈ 0.3% => apply to invoice, capped at 10%.
Ravi (Enablement): I'll phrase it: "If monthly availability falls below 99.5%, we calculate minutes below target and issue a credit equal to that fraction of the monthly bill, subject to the contract cap (e.g., 10%). Example above yields ~0.3% credit"
Maya (CSM): Good. @ops-bot please attach the KB on warm-start vs cold-start latency for the FAQ.
ops-bot: KB link attached: https://console.redwood.com/kb/latency-warmup
Ethan (SRE): Note: we'll annotate exports with UTC day boundaries and call out 2024-02-14 where us-east had a ~0.35% dip for 9 minutes (RCA: transient routing flaps).
Nora (Eng): Also adding a short blurb: automatic model fallback is considered part of normal operation and included in latency metrics; we surface when fallbacks occur in traces.
Maya (CSM): Timeline: raw exports today, one-page draft by tomorrow AM, final PDF before the customer call. Thanks all.
Ravi (Enablement): On it — will include 2 slides: SLO summary + worked credit example and one FAQ page.
